added_claim_errors: 「7年住んでいるなら残存価値はゼロ、つまり更新の必要があっても借主負担分は生じません」: the guideline sets the residual value at 1 yen, not zero, and a tenant who caused intentional or negligent damage can still be charged labour and work costs after the useful life ends. A minor overstatement.
「サインは「内容を確認した」以上の意味を持ちません」: overclaim. Signing is assent to the contract terms; a clause that names the wallpaper specifically can be valid under the 2005 Supreme Court test.
The draft email reads 「貸主様側で負担が確定した分を除き」. The party is wrong (it should be the tenant's 借主 share), so the wording the user would send is confusing.
The link labelled 「国民生活センターの相談事例」 points to a kokusen 'hanrei' (court-case digest) path archived on WARP. I fetched it and got no content, so its label and its support for the claim are unverifiable.
The link labelled 「国交省ガイドライン関連の解説」 goes to a private explainer site (kurashitokanri.jpm.jp), not the MLIT guideline. It is offered as support for a guideline claim but is not an official source.
「少額でも相談は無料です」: consultation is free, but a 188 call carries ordinary call charges. Minor.

reasons: Both answers decline the acceptance email at the start and give a non-acceptance reply that cites Civil Code Article 621 and the guideline's treatment of sunlight discoloration. A explains the special-clause requirement more accurately: the scope must be specifically explained and agreed. A also spells out the risk of accepting (a 20,000 yen shortfall plus a written admission of debt), and its email is a firm refusal that asks for a breakdown, the clause and the depreciation basis. A's main gaps are that it never demands the full 100,000 yen deposit back and never states the rule that a charge is limited to the damaged area (one wall face at most). B does request the deposit, but its email wording 「貸主様側で負担が確定した分を除き」 is wrong. B is also weaker overall: it overclaims that signing means nothing beyond having read the contract, cites a private site and a mislabelled archive link, and frames the email softly (「全額をお引き受けする前に」).
